mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% within the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST declined by more than 5% within the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable economic environment conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs within the last month indicates a strong labor market, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence rise.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 jobs within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong consumer-driven economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows > 1% MoM AND UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS grew by more than 1% month-over-month and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% quarter-over-quarter, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy combined with a slowing economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4.5% and GDPC1 growth was below 2% quarter-over-quarter.
